# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260922-1306-candidate-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-22 13:06 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-22 13:08 CDT`
- Research scope: Validate four direct Adyen restaurant and restaurant-platform customer stories.
- Queue item or vendor: `competitor:adyen`
- Methodology: Direct vendor-page validation with product, geography, deployment-scope, and recency limits preserved.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Conflicts found: 0
- Material takeaway: Adyen publishes credible named restaurant evidence for unified online/in-store payments, tokenization, franchise payout reporting, and donation flows, plus a restaurant-platform relationship with Zenchef. All four pages are vendor-authored and dated 2021-2023, so they support historical or then-current deployments rather than independently verified 2026 installed-base claims.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: JOE & THE JUICE
- Vendor: Adyen
- Product or category: Unified online, app, and in-store payments; centralized risk monitoring and payment reporting
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: enterprise
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 85%
- Confidence rationale: Adyen's named case study quotes a JOE & THE JUICE executive describing a single global interface, connected in-app and terminal payments, centralized payment data, and global safety controls.
- Source title: Joe & The Juice: Using payment technology to improve customer experience
- Source URL: https://www.adyen.com/en_GB/knowledge-hub/joe-and-the-juice
- Publisher or source owner: Adyen
- Published date, if known: 2021-02-05
- Accessed date: 2026-09-22
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The brand describes connecting ecommerce and physical-store payments so customers can pay in-app or at the terminal while the business sees performance through one back-end view.
- Product-specific evidence: Unified online and in-store payment processing, saved card details, global interface, transaction monitoring, and regional risk controls.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Vendor-authored and rooted in the 2020 pandemic period; the page does not establish current 2026 modules, contract status, location coverage, or payment volume.
- Recommended follow-up: Seek a current brand-controlled payments or expansion source and confirm 2026 geography and terminal footprint.

### Observation 2

- Brand: Domino's Netherlands
- Vendor: Adyen
- Product or category: Unified commerce payments, Sales Day Payout reporting, online and in-store payment consolidation, and fallback processing
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: The page explicitly says Domino's Netherlands chose Adyen's unified commerce solution and quotes Domino's Netherlands and Europe executives about the payment and data relationship.
- Source title: Fresh hot innovation: How Domino's perfected operational agility with unified commerce
- Source URL: https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/how-dominos-perfected-operational-agility-with-unified-commerce-payments
- Publisher or source owner: Adyen
- Published date, if known: 2021-09-02
- Accessed date: 2026-09-22
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Adyen states that Domino's Netherlands consolidated online and in-store payments and uses Sales Day Payout reporting so franchisees can reconcile sales and payouts by channel, method, and day.
- Product-specific evidence: Unified commerce, Sales Day Payout, offline/store-and-forward processing, mobile-network failover, cross-channel reporting, and customer/payment insights.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The evidence is specifically Netherlands/Europe context and must not be generalized to Domino's globally. It is vendor-authored and five years old.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current deployment with Domino's Netherlands or European franchise disclosures and determine whether the same stack remains active.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Leon
- Vendor: Adyen, integrated through Vita Mojo
- Product or category: Omnichannel payments, shopper tokenization, payment data, and Adyen Giving
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 85%
- Confidence rationale: Adyen's case study names the three-party relationship, quotes Leon and Vita Mojo leaders, and describes implemented tokenization and Giving functionality.
- Source title: Melding millennial tech demands with a fresh approach to QSR: Leon restaurants
- Source URL: https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/leon-changing-qsr-expections-
- Publisher or source owner: Adyen
- Published date, if known: 2022-05-18
- Accessed date: 2026-09-22
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Vita Mojo introduced Leon to Adyen for payments across mobile, kiosk, and ecommerce; the page says Adyen tokenization supplied repeat-visit insight and Giving was implemented at checkout.
- Product-specific evidence: Cross-channel payments, shopper tokenization, guest-frequency analytics, and terminal donation flow.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The ordering app and kiosks are attributed to Vita Mojo, not Adyen. The page's 70-location context and donation result are historical, not verified current footprint.
- Recommended follow-up: Verify the current Leon-Vita Mojo-Adyen architecture and geographic coverage through a brand-controlled or current partner source.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Zenchef
- Vendor: Adyen
- Product or category: Adyen for Platforms powering Zenchef Payments, prepayment, pre-authorization, QR pay-at-table, processing, and payment data
- Relationship indication: partner
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 90%
- Confidence rationale: Zenchef's VP of Partnerships is quoted describing the 2021 selection of Adyen, the white-label platform requirements, and the resulting Zenchef Payments capabilities.
- Source title: Zenchef and Adyen: The recipe for a successful customer experience
- Source URL: https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/zenchef-adyen-recipe-for-customer-experience
- Publisher or source owner: Adyen
- Published date, if known: 2023-08-04
- Accessed date: 2026-09-22
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: The page says Zenchef turned to Adyen in 2021, uses Adyen for Platforms for its white-label payments offering, and that Adyen processes a large proportion of Zenchef payments in France.
- Product-specific evidence: Platform payments, prepayments, card pre-authorization, QR table payments, authorization optimization, payment data, and transaction-level commercial reporting.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: This is a SaaS-platform partnership, not evidence that every one of Zenchef's 11,000 restaurant customers uses Adyen. The stated processing scope is a large proportion in France, not all Zenchef markets.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm current European rollout, restaurant adoption by market, and whether Zenchef Payments remains exclusively or primarily powered by Adyen.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: Current 2026 global enterprise deployment for each named restaurant brand.
- Pages checked: All four source pages in the ledger.
- Result: None independently establishes a current 2026 global footprint. Domino's evidence is Netherlands/Europe scoped, Leon is a three-party implementation with Vita Mojo, Zenchef is a platform relationship with partial France processing scope, and all pages are vendor-authored.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://www.adyen.com/en_GB/knowledge-hub/joe-and-the-juice | Case study | 2026-09-22 | 1 | Named executive and global-interface evidence; pandemic-period context. |
| https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/how-dominos-perfected-operational-agility-with-unified-commerce-payments | Case study | 2026-09-22 | 2 | Explicit Netherlands selection and franchise reporting; not a global Domino's claim. |
| https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/leon-changing-qsr-expections- | Case study | 2026-09-22 | 3 | Adyen payments are mediated through Vita Mojo; ordering and kiosks belong to Vita Mojo. |
| https://www.adyen.com/knowledge-hub/zenchef-adyen-recipe-for-customer-experience | Case study | 2026-09-22 | 4 | Strong platform-partnership evidence with limited France processing scope. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Adyen's restaurant-market strength appears concentrated in cross-channel payment unification, tokenized customer insight, franchise reconciliation, and embedded platform payments rather than core restaurant POS.
- Inference: The Vita Mojo and Zenchef examples show channel-partner leverage, but downstream restaurant coverage cannot be inferred without customer- or market-level evidence.
- Review instruction: Preserve the publication dates, geography, partner boundaries, and absence of independent 2026 confirmation during morning-cycle triage.
